title: Baby hip X-ray
what: An X-ray of your baby's hip joints. It shows whether the joints are formed correctly.
why: Usually after 3 to 4 months of age, when the joints show better on X-ray, if an ultrasound or an orthopedic exam raised questions.
duration: usually 5 to 10 minutes in the room; the report the same day
tell_doctor: If your baby already had a hip ultrasound or X-ray
If your baby wears a hip brace or harness. Tell the orthopedic doctor
If the mother who will be there is pregnant, another adult should go with the baby

prepare.title: Feeding
prepare.text: Feed your baby shortly before the X-ray. A full baby is calmer.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes that come off easily. Bring a clean diaper and a sheet.

prepare.title: Toy
prepare.text: A favorite toy or a pacifier will help distract your baby.

bring: A diaper, a sheet, and a pacifier or bottle
steps: You undress your baby down to the diaper. Sometimes the diaper is removed too
Your baby is laid on their back with the legs held straight
You may be given a protective apron and asked to hold your baby
A protective shield is put over the genitals, if it does not cover the joints
The image takes a fraction of a second
feel: It does not hurt your baby
Many babies cry because they are being held. This is normal and quick
after: You can dress your baby and go home right away
Take the image and report to a pediatric orthopedic doctor

faq.q: Is the radiation harmful for my baby?
faq.a: The dose is very small. The X-ray is ordered only when it is needed to decide on treatment.

faq.q: Why not an ultrasound instead of an X-ray?
faq.a: Babies up to 3 to 4 months usually have an ultrasound. Later the joints harden into bone, and an X-ray shows them better.

reminders.text: Your baby's hip X-ray is soon. Bring a diaper, a sheet, and a pacifier. Feed your baby shortly before.
